summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

F127 · FORMULA 2: Quantum simulation reference error. Candidate: e_Q=2625.4996*abs(E_Q-E_ref). Units and assumptions: Both E Hartree; factor kJ/mol per Hartree; e_Q kJ/mol. Three-dimensional interpretation: Absolute error basin over depth and shot budget. Refutation: Active-space mismatch must invalidate comparison. F127 · FORMULA 3: Finite shot variance. Candidate: Var(Ehat)=sum_j c_j^2*(1-<Pj>^2)/Nj. Units and assumptions: c_j energy; Pj dimensionless ±1; Nj counts; variance energy squared. Three-dimensional interpretation: Shot-allocation precision frontier. Refutation: Correlated measurement grouping changes variance. F127 · FORMULA 4: Depolarizing depth decay. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

F126 · FORMULA 4: Langmuir occupancy candidate. Candidate: theta=(K*C)/(1+K*C). Units and assumptions: K reciprocal concentration; C concentration, theta fraction. F127 · FORMULA 2: Quantum simulation reference error. Candidate: e_Q=2625.4996*abs(E_Q-E_ref). Units and assumptions: Both E Hartree; factor kJ/mol per Hartree; e_Q kJ/mol. Three-dimensional interpretation: Absolute error basin over depth and shot budget. Refutation: Active-space mismatch must invalidate comparison. F127 · FORMULA 3: Finite shot variance. Candidate: Var(Ehat)=sum_j c_j^2*(1-<Pj>^2)/Nj. Units and assumptions: c_j energy; Pj dimensionless ±1; Nj counts; variance energy squared. Three-dimensional interpretation: Shot-allocation precision frontier. Refutation: Correlated measurement grouping changes variance. F127 · FORMULA 4: Depolarizing depth decay. Candidate: F(depth)=F0*(1-p)^depth. Units and assumptions: p probability, depth count; F dimensionless. Three-dimensional interpretation: Depth dependence can overwhelm nominal ansatz gains. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

Three-dimensional interpretation: Reference-error ridge changes with surface coverage. Refutation: Exclude no nonconverged surface from denominator. F126 · FORMULA 3: Coverage-dependent chemical potential. Candidate: mu=mu0+R*T*ln(theta/(1-theta)). Units and assumptions: R kJ/(mol*K); T K; theta fraction 0<theta<1; mu kJ/mol. Three-dimensional interpretation: Logarithmic singularities at near-zero and near-saturation coverage. Refutation: Lateral interactions invalidate ideal lattice-gas model. F126 · FORMULA 4: Langmuir occupancy candidate. Candidate: theta=(K*C)/(1+K*C). Units and assumptions: K reciprocal concentration; C concentration, theta fraction. Three-dimensional interpretation: Basis-dependent correction ridge for localized adsorption. Refutation: A correction is not a license to ignore surface relaxation. F126 · FORMULA 6: Surface site population entropy. Candidate: Ssite=-R*sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Units and assumptions: p_i fraction summing to one; R kJ/(mol*K); S kJ/(mol*K). summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

Independent scientific witness: independent certified gas-phase/surface-reference measurement packet and blinded confidence-interval coverage audit. Concealed adversarial perturbation: sealed lab-to-lab calibration and sample-batch reversal plus artificially contaminated uncertainty labels. A rival interpretation is overwide confidence intervals, shared calibration artifacts, post hoc uncertainty tuning or selective omission of failing experimental batches. Stop if nominal confidence level undefined, denominator selectively altered, instrument not traceable, or external coverage fails preregistration. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

Units and assumptions: E terms kJ/mol for same charge/reference; negative Eads means stable adsorption only under declared convention. Three-dimensional interpretation: Adsorption-energy valley across coverage and distance. Refutation: An unmatched slab relaxation or inconsistent energy zero creates false binding. F126 · FORMULA 2: Absolute adsorption-energy benchmark. Candidate: MAEads=(1/N)*sum_i |Epred_i-Eref_i|. Units and assumptions: Energy difference kJ/mol; N independent held-out site-molecule pairs. Three-dimensional interpretation: Reference-error ridge changes with surface coverage. Refutation: Exclude no nonconverged surface from denominator. F126 · FORMULA 3: Coverage-dependent chemical potential. Candidate: mu=mu0+R*T*ln(theta/(1-theta)). Units and assumptions: R kJ/(mol*K); T K; theta fraction 0<theta<1; mu kJ/mol. Three-dimensional interpretation: Logarithmic singularities at near-zero and near-saturation coverage. Refutation: Lateral interactions invalidate ideal lattice-gas model. F126 · FORMULA 4: Langmuir occupancy candidate. Candidate: theta=(K*C)/(1+K*C). Units and assumptions: K reciprocal concentration; C concentration, theta fraction. Three-dimensional interpretation: Saturation plateau reveals site competition. Refutation: Surface heterogeneity or irreversible adsorption defeats single-site assumption. F126 · FORMULA 5: Counterpoise corrected interaction. Candidate: EintCP=EAB(AB)-EA(ABghost)-EB(AghostB). Units and assumptions: All energies same kJ/mol basis/geometry convention. Three-dimensional interpretation: Basis-dependent correction ridge for localized adsorption. Refutation: A correction is not a license to ignore surface relaxation. F126 · FORMULA 6: Surface site population entropy. Candidate: Ssite=-R*sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Units and assumptions: p_i fraction summing to one; R kJ/(mol*K); S kJ/(mol*K). Three-dimensional interpretation: Site-disorder basin changes free-energy inference. Refutation: Unobserved adsorption sites invalidate population normalization. F127 · FORMULA 1: Variational energy bound. Candidate: Evar=<psi|H|psi>/<psi|psi>. Units and assumptions: Hamiltonian consistent energy units; quotient energy (Hartree). Three-dimensional interpretation: Ansatz-depth energy landscape may trap optimization. Refutation: Hardware noise can violate ideal bound interpretation. F127 · FORMULA 2: Quantum simulation reference error. Candidate: e_Q=2625.4996*abs(E_Q-E_ref). Units and assumptions: Both E Hartree; factor kJ/mol per Hartree; e_Q kJ/mol. Three-dimensional interpretation: Absolute error basin over depth and shot budget. Refutation: Active-space mismatch must invalidate comparison. F127 · FORMULA 3: Finite shot variance. Candidate: Var(Ehat)=sum_j c_j^2*(1-<Pj>^2)/Nj. Units and assumptions: c_j energy; Pj dimensionless ±1; Nj counts; variance energy squared. Three-dimensional interpretation: Shot-allocation precision frontier. Refutation: Correlated measurement grouping changes variance. F127 · FORMULA 4: Depolarizing depth decay. Candidate: F(depth)=F0*(1-p)^depth. Units and assumptions: p probability, depth count; F dimensionless. Three-dimensional interpretation: Depth dependence can overwhelm nominal ansatz gains. Refutation: Compilation changes effective noise model. F127 · FORMULA 5: Mitigation overhead ratio. Candidate: Omit=C_mitigated/C_raw. Units and assumptions: Both costs same wall-time or energy unit; ratio dimensionless. Three-dimensional interpretation: Error-cost frontier may reverse winner. Refutation: Ignoring calibration overhead invents advantage. F127 · FORMULA 6: Matched budget advantage. Candidate: A_Q=(e_classical-e_Q)/B. Units and assumptions: Errors kJ/mol; B CPU-equivalent hours or stated budget; result kJ/(mol*hour). Three-dimensional interpretation: Resource-normalized advantage surface. Refutation: Different hardware energy or workflow definitions invalidate B. F128 · FORMULA 1: Isomer identification accuracy. Candidate: Accuracy=100*Ncorrect/Ntest. Units and assumptions: Count denominator blind authenticated isomers; %. Three-dimensional interpretation: Resolution-coverage detection ridge. Refutation: Leakage from library identities inflates apparent accuracy. F128 · FORMULA 2: Balanced isomer class accuracy. Candidate: BAcc=100*mean_k(TPk/(TPk+FNk)). No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. F122 / Conformational Energy Landscapes of Botanical Terpenes at the Limit The proposed physical object is ranking of torsional conformers in complex botanical terpene stereoisomers, with emphasis on torsional potential energy, conformer search coverage, Boltzmann populations, thermal barriers, stereo- and enantiomer assignment, correlated energy errors and duplicated minima. Primary decision: Conformer rank agreement (Kendall tau) [ratio]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs authenticated cis/trans and enantiomeric terpene structures, archived conformer search seeds and blinded reference-energy sets. Compare to exhaustive classical conformer search followed by the same high-level electronic reference and preregistered rank agreement. An independent observer must evaluate independent deduplicated conformer geometries, high-level relative energies and tie-aware Kendall tau calculated on withheld structures. Blinded adversarial intervention: hidden mirror-image stereoisomer and duplicate-conformer injection before blinded re-ranking. Potentially stronger rival: undersampled conformers, duplicate conformer labels or biased tie treatment falsely improving agreement. Hard stop: unresolved stereoisomer identity, insufficient conformer coverage, unstable ranking under resampling or ill-defined Kendall tau denominator. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F122, the strongest classical analysis may win. Primary decision: Receptor-binding energy prediction MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs documented synthetic ligand-pocket cluster coordinates, archived reference structures and separately labelled hypothetical receptor conformations. Compare to matched classical force-field plus high-level cluster quantum chemistry with explicit solvation controls and an independent binding reference if available. An independent observer must evaluate holdout geometry and binding-energy benchmark with independent structural annotation and environmental assumptions. Blinded adversarial intervention: blind receptor-pocket rotamer and protonation swap with a decoy ligand of identical size. Potentially stronger rival: docking pose selection or solvent/protonation mismatch yielding attractive computed energies without genuine binding. Hard stop: undefined receptor structure or protonation, no legitimate reference binding energy, uncorrected double-counting or model interpreting binding as sensory effect. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F123, the strongest classical analysis may win. F124 / Quantum Chemistry of Essential-Oil Oxidation Pathways at the Limit The proposed physical object is oxidative transition states and competing reaction pathways for terpene constituents, with emphasis on radical initiation, oxygen addition, hydrogen transfer, conformer-dependent transition states, spin-state crossings, intrinsic reaction coordinates, zero-point corrections and branching competing channels. Primary decision: Oxidation transition-state energy error [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally defined terpene oxidation reactants, radicals and transition-state coordinate sets; no synthesized reactive intermediates. Compare to same-stationary-point reference transition-state energies using established electronic-structure methods with vibrational and IRC verification. An independent observer must evaluate independent harmonic frequency/IRC files, matched reaction states, oxygen accounting and high-level reference barrier energies. Blinded adversarial intervention: withheld spin-state and competing oxygen-addition channel with randomized path labels. Potentially stronger rival: wrong saddle order, missing radical branch, inconsistent spin reference or mismatched zero-point energy. Hard stop: transition structure without one valid imaginary mode and connected IRC, unaccounted oxygen stoichiometry or severe reference-state mismatch. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F124, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F125 / Photochemical Degradation of Aroma Molecules at the Limit The proposed physical object is light-driven transformation rates, absorption cross sections and competing oxygen pathways, with emphasis on wavelength-dependent photon absorption, excited-state quantum yield, oxygen-quenching, radical photoproduct branches, nonradiative loss and dark-reaction baselines. Primary decision: Photochemical degradation rate coefficient [h^-1]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs traceable simulated terpene chromophores, documented absorption spectra and synthetic photon flux distributions with reference lamp metadata. Hard stop: unmeasured lamp spectrum, missing parent-plus-photoproduct balance, nonidentified reaction rate or unstable photon-dose calibration. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F125, the strongest classical analysis may win. Units: All energies kJ/mol; N distinct held-out molecules; MAE kJ/mol. 3D: An error basin whose apparently low corner may omit difficult structures. F121 / Variational state energy: E_var = <psi|H|psi>/<psi|psi>. Units: Numerator energy in Hartree and denominator dimensionless; E_var Hartree. 3D: A variational saddle reflects ansatz expressivity, not quantum advantage. F121 / Basis-set extrapolation: E(X) = E_inf + A*X^(-3). Units: E and A Hartree; cardinal X dimensionless; single-reference asymptotic assumption. 3D: A convergence ridge flattening as X rises. F121 / Molecular energy error uncertainty: u_diff = sqrt(u_calc^2+u_ref^2-2*cov). Units: Both uncertainties Hartree; covariance Hartree^2; u_diff Hartree. 3D: An uncertainty contour may hide correlated reference errors. F121 / Energy improvement per compute cost: G = (MAE_ref-MAE_new)/Cost. Units: Numerator kJ/mol; cost CPU-hour/molecule; G kJ*mol^-1/(CPU-hour/molecule). 3D: The gain-cost ridge may reverse under a full compute budget. F122 / Periodic torsion potential: V(phi)=V0+sum[V_n*(1+cos(n*phi-delta_n))/2]. Units: V0,Vn kJ/mol; phi and phase in radians inside cosine; V kJ/mol. 3D: Periodic torsional ridges identify alternate basins. F122 / Boltzmann conformer probability: p_i=exp(-DeltaE_i/(R*T))/Z. F123 / Conformational ensemble binding free energy: DeltaG_eff=-R*T*ln(sum_i p_i*exp(-DeltaG_i/(R*T))). Units: R kJ/(mol*K), T K, G kJ/mol; p_i normalized. 3D: A multi-pocket basin changes under ensemble reweighting. F123 / Binding entropy correction: DeltaG=DeltaH-T*DeltaS. Units: DeltaH kJ/mol; DeltaS kJ/(mol*K); T K; DeltaG kJ/mol. 3D: Entropy term produces a temperature-dependent saddle. F123 / Binding prediction normalized error: z=(G_pred-G_ref)/u_G. Units: G and uncertainty u_G kJ/mol; z dimensionless. 3D: A standardized residual frontier diagnoses false confidence. F124 / Oxidation activation barrier: DeltaE_dagger=E_TS-E_reactants. Units: E_TS and E_reactants kJ/mol with same charge/spin and ZPE convention. 3D: A reaction coordinate saddle must be independently verified. F124 / Transition barrier prediction error: epsilon_TS=DeltaE_dagger,pred-DeltaE_dagger,ref. Units: Both barriers kJ/mol in matching reference convention; error kJ/mol. 3D: A basis-dependent error valley can hide missing reaction channels. F124 / Eyring transition state rate: k=(kB*T/h)*exp(-DeltaG_dagger/(R*T)). Units: kB*T/h s^-1; DeltaG_dagger and RT J/mol; k s^-1. 3D: Rate curvature amplifies modest barrier differences. F124 / Activation free-energy identity: DeltaG_dagger=DeltaH_dagger-T*DeltaS_dagger. Units: DeltaH J/mol; DeltaS J/(mol*K); T K; result J/mol. 3D: Entropy-driven crossing shows why electronic barrier is not Gibbs barrier. F124 / Reaction branching fraction: f_i=k_i/sum_j(k_j). Units: All competing rate constants in same time unit; f dimensionless. 3D: Competing channels make ridges instead of a single preferred path. F124 / Vibrational saddle requirement: N_imag(TS)=1. Units: Count of imaginary harmonic frequencies; dimensionless integer. 3D: A discrete topology gate, not a smooth empirical surface. F125 / Apparent first-order photolysis rate: k_app=-d[ln(C/C0)]/dt. Units: C and C0 same units; t h; k_app h^-1, only within first-order regime. 3D: Decay-rate ridge must match independent parent/product inventory. F125 / Photon-flux photolysis kernel: k_photo=3600*integral(phi(lam)*sigma(lam)*F(lam)dlam). Units: Quantum yield phi dimensionless; sigma m2; spectral photon flux integrated photons/(m2*s); k h^-1. 3D: Action-spectrum crest follows wavelength-resolved absorption. F125 / Beer-Lambert optical absorbance: A=epsilon*c*l. Units: epsilon L/(mol*cm), c mol/L, l cm; absorbance dimensionless. 3D: Absorbance saturation ridge violates linear small-signal expectation. F125 / Molecular photolysis quantum yield: phi=N_reacted/N_absorbed. Units: Photon and reacted molecule counts; phi dimensionless in simple one-photon pathway. 3D: Yield valley tests competing relaxation channels. F125 / Integrated photon fluence: H_photon=integral(F_photon(t) dt). Units: F photons/(m2*s); dt s; fluence photons/m2. 3D: Fluence contours expose different intensity-time schedules. F125 / Photo-dark competing reaction rates: k_total=k_photo+k_dark+k_oxygen. Units: All k in h^-1 for same parent species and valid first-order approximation. 3D: Oxygen-pressure saddle distinguishes independent reaction paths. summary: STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW ERA / FAMILY 25 / F121-F125 QUANTUM CHEMISTRY OF BOTANICAL AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH WORKING EDITION V1.0 / PROSPECTIVE, NONCLINICAL, FALSIFIABLE, NUMERICALLY REPRODUCIBLE SCIENTIFIC IDENTITY AND NONCLAIM BOUNDARY Family 25 invites future molecular researchers to test five distinct hypotheses: electronic-structure reference accuracy, stereochemically resolved conformer ranking, conditional ligand and olfactory receptor interaction energies, oxidation transition-state errors, and wavelength-dependent photochemical degradation rates. Each question has a different kind of observable. F121, F123 and F124 require energy-error units in kJ/mol; F122 requires dimensionless Kendall rank agreement; F125 uses h^-1 for a first-order kinetic coefficient. Shared molecular metadata cannot make these numerical quantities interchangeable. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional meshes visualize possibilities, not results computed for an actual terpene. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. FIVE INDIVIDUAL FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F121 / Quantum-Chemical Simulation of Aroma Electronic Structure at the Limit The proposed physical object is electronic-structure prediction of authenticated botanical odorant molecules, with emphasis on electron correlation, density functional approximation, basis-set incompleteness, spin state, reference geometry, stereochemistry, pseudopotential choice and convergence diagnostics. Primary decision: Electronic structure energy MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally identified terpene molecular graphs, stereochemical identifiers, reproducible geometries and frozen quantum chemistry input files. Compare to same-geometry high-level classical quantum chemistry, where feasible DLPNO-CCSD(T) or carefully converged reference calculations under a registered resource budget. An independent observer must evaluate independently generated matched-geometry high-level electronic-energy tables with computational settings, provenance and uncertainty. Blinded adversarial intervention: blinded stereoisomer-label permutation with a concealed basis-set and geometry swap. Potentially stronger rival: conformer omission, changed reference geometry or inconsistent electronic reference state rather than an improved Hamiltonian approximation. Hard stop: missing independent energy reference, uncontrolled charge or spin, nonconvergent SCF or undisclosed multi-reference character. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F121, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. Primary decision: Conformer rank agreement (Kendall tau) [ratio]. EIGHTY-TWO PROGRESSIVE CHAPTERS / THE SIX-PASSAGE SCIENTIFIC METHOD Every chapter begins with a different molecular uncertainty and travels through six progressively stronger gates of evidence. The first passage defines chemical identity and valid reference state. The second states a dimensional mechanism and coordinates on which it could be false. The third freezes independent benchmarks and uncertainty. The fourth injects an unseen competitor. The fifth hands the protocol to an uncoached external quantum-chemistry group. The sixth preserves failed input decks and a binding stopping rule. Every one of the 492 passages contains Mechanism, Measurement and Refutation; the three roles are scientifically different and never turn a model image into a measurement. The full notebook retains the individual chapter arguments, including negative conditions and resource accounting. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. F121, F123 and F124 require energy-error units in kJ/mol; F122 requires dimensionless Kendall rank agreement; F125 uses h^-1 for a first-order kinetic coefficient. Shared molecular metadata cannot make these numerical quantities interchangeable. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional meshes visualize possibilities, not results computed for an actual terpene. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally identified terpene molecular graphs, stereochemical identifiers, reproducible geometries and frozen quantum chemistry input files. Compare to same-geometry high-level classical quantum chemistry, where feasible DLPNO-CCSD(T) or carefully converged reference calculations under a registered resource budget. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. F121, F123 and F124 require energy-error units in kJ/mol; F122 requires dimensionless Kendall rank agreement; F125 uses h^-1 for a first-order kinetic coefficient. Shared molecular metadata cannot make these numerical quantities interchangeable. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional meshes visualize possibilities, not results computed for an actual terpene. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer.
