summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

direction_title: Memory Cortex: new source-grounded retrieval and continual-memory research [FORWARD]
summary: This replication package accompanies the study of Norgespris, Norway's voluntary fixed-price electricity scheme. The paper compares electricity meters that entered the scheme early with meters classified as non-adopters in three southern Norwegian bidding zones (NO1, NO2 and NO5) from October 2023 to April 2026. It examines who stood to gain from fixed-price protection, how the cohorts responded to daily electricity prices before and after adoption, and how their relative consumption changed. The archive includes aggregate hourly consumption and meter counts from Elhub, ERA5 temperature data obtained through Open-Meteo, and the Python and R code used to generate the tables, figures and numerical results in the paper and its supplement. The README gives the software versions, the command for running the analysis, and a guide to the files behind each exhibit. The included retrieval script obtains the hourly electricity prices from Hva koster strømmen and checks all 2,829 supplier responses against their archived SHA-256 digests.
title: Who Gives Up the Price Signal? Selection, Price Responsiveness and Demand under Norway's Voluntary Fixed Electricity Price

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

Units and assumptions: E terms kJ/mol for same charge/reference; negative Eads means stable adsorption only under declared convention. Three-dimensional interpretation: Adsorption-energy valley across coverage and distance. Refutation: An unmatched slab relaxation or inconsistent energy zero creates false binding. F126 · FORMULA 2: Absolute adsorption-energy benchmark. Candidate: MAEads=(1/N)*sum_i |Epred_i-Eref_i|. Units and assumptions: Energy difference kJ/mol; N independent held-out site-molecule pairs. Three-dimensional interpretation: Reference-error ridge changes with surface coverage. Refutation: Exclude no nonconverged surface from denominator. F126 · FORMULA 3: Coverage-dependent chemical potential. Candidate: mu=mu0+R*T*ln(theta/(1-theta)). Units and assumptions: R kJ/(mol*K); T K; theta fraction 0<theta<1; mu kJ/mol. Three-dimensional interpretation: Logarithmic singularities at near-zero and near-saturation coverage. Refutation: Lateral interactions invalidate ideal lattice-gas model. F126 · FORMULA 4: Langmuir occupancy candidate. Candidate: theta=(K*C)/(1+K*C). Units and assumptions: K reciprocal concentration; C concentration, theta fraction. Three-dimensional interpretation: Saturation plateau reveals site competition. Refutation: Surface heterogeneity or irreversible adsorption defeats single-site assumption. F126 · FORMULA 6: Surface site population entropy. Candidate: Ssite=-R*sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Units and assumptions: p_i fraction summing to one; R kJ/(mol*K); S kJ/(mol*K). Three-dimensional interpretation: Site-disorder basin changes free-energy inference. Refutation: Unobserved adsorption sites invalidate population normalization. F127 · FORMULA 1: Variational energy bound. Candidate: Evar=<psi|H|psi>/<psi|psi>. Units and assumptions: Hamiltonian consistent energy units; quotient energy (Hartree). Three-dimensional interpretation: Ansatz-depth energy landscape may trap optimization. Refutation: Hardware noise can violate ideal bound interpretation. F127 · FORMULA 2: Quantum simulation reference error. Candidate: e_Q=2625.4996*abs(E_Q-E_ref). Units and assumptions: Both E Hartree; factor kJ/mol per Hartree; e_Q kJ/mol. Three-dimensional interpretation: Absolute error basin over depth and shot budget. Refutation: Active-space mismatch must invalidate comparison. F127 · FORMULA 3: Finite shot variance. Candidate: Var(Ehat)=sum_j c_j^2*(1-<Pj>^2)/Nj. Units and assumptions: c_j energy; Pj dimensionless ±1; Nj counts; variance energy squared. Three-dimensional interpretation: Shot-allocation precision frontier. Refutation: Correlated measurement grouping changes variance. F127 · FORMULA 4: Depolarizing depth decay. Candidate: F(depth)=F0*(1-p)^depth. Units and assumptions: p probability, depth count; F dimensionless. Three-dimensional interpretation: Depth dependence can overwhelm nominal ansatz gains. Each question has a different kind of observable. F121, F123 and F124 require energy-error units in kJ/mol; F122 requires dimensionless Kendall rank agreement; F125 uses h^-1 for a first-order kinetic coefficient. Shared molecular metadata cannot make these numerical quantities interchangeable. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional meshes visualize possibilities, not results computed for an actual terpene. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. Primary decision: Electronic structure energy MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally identified terpene molecular graphs, stereochemical identifiers, reproducible geometries and frozen quantum chemistry input files. Compare to same-geometry high-level classical quantum chemistry, where feasible DLPNO-CCSD(T) or carefully converged reference calculations under a registered resource budget. An independent observer must evaluate independently generated matched-geometry high-level electronic-energy tables with computational settings, provenance and uncertainty. Blinded adversarial intervention: blinded stereoisomer-label permutation with a concealed basis-set and geometry swap. Potentially stronger rival: conformer omission, changed reference geometry or inconsistent electronic reference state rather than an improved Hamiltonian approximation. Hard stop: missing independent energy reference, uncontrolled charge or spin, nonconvergent SCF or undisclosed multi-reference character. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F121, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. direction_title: Memory Cortex: new source-grounded retrieval and continual-memory research [FORWARD]
summary: Abstract. Spin-independent mα⁶ operators of lithium require singular three-electron Hylleraas integrals. We classify all supports of eight selected operator representations, obtaining 21 negative patterns, 12 finite-part families and 58 finite-part minimal rows. Every such row has four rational seed coordinates and an explicit polylogarithmic remainder. Generic non-isogeny and product monodromy make these coordinates unique; exactly 5 minimal rows are elliptic. Every reached pattern has a published treatment or a finite representation, with at most two residual variables where needed. A closed-form atlas of 98 functions includes 291 wall formulas and 174 ray formulas. The evaluator covers positive exact rational exponents; 1044 values at 18 points agree with independent evaluations of the formulas to 40 significant digits. At 9 further pre-specified points, all 522 values agree with an independent implementation of the same closed forms in every printed digit. Independent native quadratures confirm sampled values to 55 digits or more at 5 points spanning all four chambers. We compare 231 published reference values and classify the differences. A worked Q₄₄ matrix element proves that total basis degree three is the lowest admitting an element outside the algebraic-letter polylogarithmic class. Open questions include unresolved cone classifications, a smaller lower-function space on triangle walls, a complete seed form for the worked element, and missing native values. This record holds the manuscript (version 7; 53 pages), the verification bundle LITHIUM_QED_MASTER_P3_v7.zip (LaTeX source and PDF, the supplementary verification package with the census atlas, the wall and ray formulas, the selected representations, value tables, published-value comparisons, the unchanged closed-form evaluator and the replay script run_checks.py , the fact sheet and claim map that tie every statement to its source, and the provenance of the manuscript; 505 files, checked by MANIFEST.sha256 ), the clean arXiv LaTeX source, and SHA256SUMS.txt . README.md explains how to verify the files and run the checks; PAPER3_VERIFICATION/README.md inside the bundle is the entry point for the replay. The code is under the MIT licence; the manuscript and the data are under CC BY 4.0. Companion articles: J. Matuzas, Elliptic structure of the singular three-electron Hylleraas integrals, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23917908 ; J. Matuzas, Three-electron Hylleraas integrals with two inverse-square distances: exact reduction and high-precision evaluation for the fine structure of lithium, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23977551 . Generative-AI disclosure and author responsibility. ChatGPT-6 Pro (GPT-6 Astra Pro in writing the manuscript) was used for derivations, computations, and drafting; OpenAI Codex ran the independent native computations and the independent evaluator tests on a local server; Claude Opus 5.5, with Claude Fable 5.2 in parts of the census review and of the evaluator tests, was used for independent re-derivation and audit of every increment and proposed several of the checks. summary: Abstract. Spin-independent mα⁶ operators of lithium require singular three-electron Hylleraas integrals. We classify all supports of eight selected operator representations, obtaining 21 negative patterns, 12 finite-part families and 58 finite-part minimal rows. Every such row has four rational seed coordinates and an explicit polylogarithmic remainder. Generic non-isogeny and product monodromy make these coordinates unique; exactly 5 minimal rows are elliptic. Every reached pattern has a published treatment or a finite representation, with at most two residual variables where needed. A closed-form atlas of 98 functions includes 291 wall formulas and 174 ray formulas. The evaluator covers positive exact rational exponents; 1044 values at 18 points agree with independent evaluations of the formulas to 40 significant digits. At 9 further pre-specified points, all 522 values agree with an independent implementation of the same closed forms in every printed digit. Independent native quadratures confirm sampled values to 55 digits or more at 5 points spanning all four chambers. We compare 231 published reference values and classify the differences. A worked Q₄₄ matrix element proves that total basis degree three is the lowest admitting an element outside the algebraic-letter polylogarithmic class. Open questions include unresolved cone classifications, a smaller lower-function space on triangle walls, a complete seed form for the worked element, and missing native values. A useful 4D aroma civilization must know when not to release any molecule. It must measure the real power consumed by ventilation, protect accessible withdrawal of consent, resist stale sensors, document reference material identities and preserve digital-twin state and uncertainty for future reconstruction. Complete CSV equality alone cannot prove any environmental benefit. Future investigators may replace a sophisticated controller with a cheaper conventional system and publish the negative result. Consent, source authorization, safe indoor air and physical emergency shutdown are hard constraints. summary: In multireference alignment one observes noisy copies of a signal in R^d, each cyclically shifted by an unknown random amount. The quasi maximum likelihood estimator aligns the observations jointly and averages them. Its power spectrum is biased, and Bandeira asked whether its Fourier phases are consistent once the power spectrum is corrected. They are not. Take d equal to 6, 7, 10 or 11 and the truth a unit sinusoid of frequency one. At every sufficiently large fixed noise level, the phase of the first Fourier coefficient of the estimate converges to the set of midpoints between consecutive shifts of the true phase. If the Fourier magnitudes of the estimate are then replaced by the true ones, its distance to the nearest shift of the truth converges to 2 sin(π/(2d)). The same failure holds on an open set of signals whose nonconstant Fourier coefficients are all nonzero. The deciding sign is that of an explicit Gaussian integral, which we enclose in rigorous bounds for every d from 3 to 11.
title: A half-step phase error of the hard-alignment estimator in multireference alignment

summary: Synthetic operational databases from process-based business simulation are commonly judged by resemblance to real data, which misses plausible records that could not have arisen from the process they represent. We define business-rule admissibility as the property that every state and every change in a dataset could have been produced by the represented process under its own rules, decompose it into ten criteria, each checkable as a query over a database and its change history, and name three layers where a simulation can lose it. We draw 22 cases from developing NAILU, a framework that turns business prose into executable simulations. Separate language-model agents built a study firm from its handbook; another, seeing neither the model nor its data, wrote the firm’s rules. Of nine past defects re-injected, the rules caught six in every run; seven event-log distances caught two in every run, one of them missed by the rules, and a third in most runs; the firm’s management indicators caught one only when read monthly with measures the author added, and none under a robust score. A pre-registered replication on twenty new seeds confirmed all five predictions. Of five further defects, covering a forbidden transition, recording and execution, the rules caught three in every run and one in half; one that dropped writes from the change history escaped every detector but its reconciliation with the tables. On the unchanged firm, the rules found six departures from its handbook. The evidence comes from one framework, where the detectors saw different defects
title: Business-Rule Admissibility in Process-Based Business Simulation

summary: This a research program titled the "Triple Interface Method". Its aim is to solve the Goldbach conjecture.  This manuscript presents a modular tripartite “engine” for tackling the binary Goldbach problem. The argument is broken into a small set of auditable modules—how energy is spread across rational frequencies, how bilinear short-shift correlations are controlled, how nuisance low-frequency effects are cancelled, and how average positivity is converted into pointwise positivity for every even number in a range. Each outputs a quantitative bound; together they feed a simple closing ledger that leaves only mild, standard number-theory inputs (distribution in very small moduli and a positive main term) and a routine finite base. The machinery of the paper has been coded in Lean 4 and the repo is available to the public. This proof strategy was not successful. It is preserved here for the purposes of the archive.
title: Goldbach and the Triple Interface Method

summary: GHC compares successful rewrite rules in arrival order. We ask when changing how rules are tried preserves the chosen rewrite. If every match of a later strict challenger implies a match of its earlier incumbent, a depth-first search gives a faithful first-match priority in linear time once the comparisons are known. Appending a challenger preserves old relative priorities. Inserting a structural rule before $t$ old arrivals can force almost all $\binom{t}{2}$ suffix pairs to reverse, even if the new rule never wins. An inherited list can need quadratically many reversals with only one later arrival. Given the caller table, minimum repair takes polynomial time for fixed $t$. For insertion at the head the decision problem is NP-complete even when every old rule can still win. The containment criterion covers sixteen shipped list-fold rules, including three with cyclic pairwise choices. For a fixed arrival order, testing whether the last rule can be deleted takes polynomial time on a forest of forward comparisons and is coNP-complete at treewidth two, even with disjoint one-to-one match prerequisites. Deciding whether one first-match priority preserves all winners takes polynomial time at width two and is coNP-complete at width three. For a list of $q$ possible winners, a width-two algorithm has an exponent linear in $q$, with a matching conditional lower bound. Typed Core templates realize the reductions at the GHC 9.14.1 matcher. A separate joint-order problem becomes NP-complete at three successes per call. The fold example compares the source-level work of shared tests.
title: Which GHC Rewrite Rules Can Win?

summary: Abstract Biological semiosis is a relational hypothesis whose attribution depends on evidence, causal explanation and an explicit interpretive theory. Elementary Semiotic Events provides an episode-level procedure for evaluating this inference. Each claim specifies a candidate sign, object, interpreting system and interpretant, alongside the observations and warrants linking them. Four obligations govern assessment: define the theory-relative relation, establish its biological premises, test the inferential bridge independently and evaluate rivals. ESE distinguishes formal derivability, empirical support and permission to make a theoretical attribution. Its three-valued readiness policy records failed, unresolved or satisfied obligations; chronological traces preserve the availability of evidence; and a finite-model criterion tests identifiability. Constructed examples show how a selective response can leave reference unsettled and observationally equivalent mechanisms can disagree under intervention. Transcription factor–DNA (TF–DNA) recognition provides a tractable molecular specialization, connecting sequence models, binding, regulation and interpretant hypotheses through distinct measurements. These results establish conditional properties of explicit assessment procedures and identify possible discriminating biological tests. ESE makes the premises, limits and revision conditions of a biological sign claim inspectable. Record contents This version contains the author preprint (not peer reviewed), Online Resource 1 (supplementary information) and Online Resource 2 (computational reference supplement). Online Resource 2 provides a reference implementation, deterministic tests, expected results and a checksum manifest for finite formal and synthetic claims; it contains no empirical molecular dataset and does not adjudicate biological semiosis. summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π(x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half (π), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. summary: INTEGRATED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH AT THE LIMIT F196–F200 · STARLI · White Rainbow Era · Research Working Edition v1.0 Prospective research essence | Nonclinical | Synthetic mathematical models At the end of forty integrated families, the central question changes. How can a research civilization connect five kinds of evidence while preserving the right to disagree? Family 40 gathers AI–nanorobot coordination, bioelectric and quantum sensing, philosophical and physical dual-track validation, bounded autonomous platforms, and open negative-case reconstruction. The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field. The volume offers thirty inherited candidate relationships, forty-two open numerical models, eighty-two staged chapter investigations, two hundred research doors, and thirty-three successor prototype sketches. Its deepest ambition is methodological: to make a future researcher more capable of falsifying it than the original author could have been. direction_title: Memory Cortex: new source-grounded retrieval and continual-memory research [REVERSE]
summary: Printing a floating-point number and reading it back should recover its bits. We find exactly 626,159 positive finite binary64 values whose shortest CPython spelling SQLite 3.54.1 reads as a neighbor. These failures collapse disjoint adjacent pairs. SQLite's default writer reverses 5,084 of those pairs. On each, SQLite reads its own text back to the stored value, while correct rounding gives its neighbor. We count them by locating incorrect midpoint decisions and identifying which decimals CPython can print. A repair adds 104 bytes to SQLite's power table and gives correct rounding for every 64-bit coefficient passed to the converter. Compiled versions with wide and portable multiplication agreed with exact rounding in 2,402,440 selected cases. A separate limit arises before conversion. Two 20-digit decimals can require different answers even when the scanner retains the same prefix and discards a nonzero digit from both. We determine exactly how many binary rounding boundaries remain ambiguous as additional decimal digits are retained. An exact suffix comparison and a correction to exponent accumulation give a complete reader for accepted ASCII decimals below the stated length limit. It matched whole-text rounding on 1,296,347 native tests. An x86-64 Linux build on the same Mac reproduced all five native output streams in each of seven cohorts. The complete Linux reader matched the reference on all 55,670 additional public input rows. The released reader misrounded 157 public test spellings. REAL-column import also changed 910 negative zeros to positive zero. SQLite's 18-digit format preserves every finite nonzero value with either reader.
title: Decimal Prefix Ambiguity and Binary64 Rounding in SQLite

summary: This artifact accompanies the poster paper "Evaluating Multi-Agent Incident Response: Baseline Design, Efficiency, and Policy Compliance" by Ebelechukwu Nwafor and Habeeb Olufowobi, accepted at the ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC '27). The paper asks whether a multi-agent LLM workflow for incident response is more efficient than a single agent, and shows that the answer depends on how the single-agent baseline is built. It evaluates MAN-IDS, a four-role LLM workflow, against single-agent baselines and a deterministic rule in three controlled studies on a Docker test network with Redis and PostgreSQL access scenarios. Contents - The MAN-IDS system and the evaluation harness (runners, scoring, decision protocol). - All prompts, model versions, and settings used in the studies. - The protocol for each study, written before any model calls were made. - Complete run records with full traces for 1,152 scheduled investigations across 64 campaigns:   - Study 1: explicit response policy, Claude Sonnet 5, 384 runs.   - Study 2: detector gating and routing repair, Claude Sonnet 5, 512 runs.   - Study 3: replication with Qwen3-8B on fresh campaigns, 256 runs. - Analysis scripts and their saved outputs, including the stage-timing, format-versus-decision, and comparable-quality re-analyses reported in the paper. - The trace analysis that motivated the routing repair, with the run records of the earlier evaluation it reads. - Detector experiment outputs (splits, predictions, reports) derived from CICIDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018. - The test-network setup (Docker Compose files, topology, schemas). Reproducing the results No model calls or API keys are needed. Running "python3 reproduce_analyses.py" re-runs the three study analyses from the saved run records and reports whether each result matches the shipped file byte for byte. The README lists the required Python packages and the remaining commands. Notes - Response actions were never executed. All tools are controlled and non-executing. - The public datasets are not redistributed. Only derived splits, predictions, and reports are included. - Run traces contain the absolute file paths of the machines that produced them. - Re-running the model studies would require an Anthropic API key (Studies 1 and 2) or a GPU serving Qwen3-8B (Study 3), plus Docker. title: Artifact for "Evaluating Multi-Agent Incident Response: Baseline Design, Efficiency, and Policy Compliance" (ACM SAC 2027)

summary: This record registers, before any per-origin value was read, a test of how three checkpoint-relief alleles combine at individual budding-yeast replication origins. The data are the eight-genotype factorials of Sheu, Kinney and Stillman (2016, Genome Research 26:315–330), taken from the authors' repository (github.com/jbkinney/14_sheu, commit 026c2ef). The primary test uses the 0.2 M HU, 90-min factorial. The 0.05% MMS factorial serves as an agreement test, and the unperturbed 25-min factorial as a negative control. A triple-mutant HU time course, run in two separate experiments, supplies the HU noise estimate. Product, additive and constrained stochastic-threshold models are compared in a single censored likelihood. Each sample carries its own scale and floor. Three gates come first: a replicate control, an unperturbed null and an information check. A verdict requires agreement across floor treatments, width adjustment, doubled noise and the MMS condition. Every verdict is provisional pending a replicated HU factorial. The design corrects three errors in the earlier Pol α registration (10.5281/zenodo.24450406): a missing scale term, a floor treated as exact, and an ambiguous reference level. Version 2 adds Amendment 1, filed before any per-origin value was read: the condition assignment is confirmed from figure captions and per-sample settings because Supplemental Table 1 is not accessible; floor treatment F1 is recomputed from the repository profiles; and a second HU 90-min replicate gate (set 7 vs set 4) is added. Version 3 deposits the outcome. The registered analysis terminated at Gate 3, the unperturbed negative control: three of four interaction terms exceeded the registered threshold with the checkpoint inactive (mcm4Δ74-174 × dbf4-19A γ = 1.40, 95% CI 0.98–1.85). The registered outcome is uninterpretable, and the HU combination-rule comparison was not performed. Gates 2, 2b and 4 passed. Code and outputs reproduce every reported number from the authors' repository (commit 026c2ef).
title: Prospective registration: combination rules for sld3-38A, dbf4-19A and mcm4Δ74-174 at individual replication origins in the Sheu et al. (2016) factorial

summary: Data and analysis files supporting Salichos et al., Multi-host phylodynamics of hepatitis E virus reveals extensive lineage sharing across humans, wild boar, and swine . The study analysed 436 hepatitis E virus ORF2 sequences from humans, wild boar, swine and camels, together with 49 ICTV subtype reference genomes. Subtypes were reassigned de novo by phylogenetic placement, and time-calibrated coalescent and birth–death skyline analyses were run for 13 subtype- and host-specific datasets, followed by a discrete-trait analysis of host transitions among HEV-3 lineages. This deposit contains the 411 bp alignment and per-analysis alignments with sampling dates, sequence metadata after filtering and deduplication, BEAST v2.7.7 XML input files, parameter log files, the annotated maximum clade credibility and maximum-likelihood trees shown in the figures, and the scripts used for the temporal-signal testing, the host and subtype rate comparison, and Figures 2 and 4. All sequences are publicly available in GenBank; accession numbers are listed in alignments/metadata.tsv . Results tables are published with the article and are not duplicated here. See README.md for the full contents. Version 2 adds three analyses, in HEV_round2_additions.tgz. All version 1 files are unchanged. prior_sens/ — Sensitivity of the becoming-uninfectious rate (δ) to its prior. summary: This record contains the code, the processed input data and the results of every run of a benchmark study on the day-ahead and rolling-horizon scheduling of building energy systems with photovoltaics (PV), photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) collectors, a battery, a heat pump and a thermal storage tank.   The study compares three quantum-inspired metaheuristics (quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm, quantum-behaved particle swarm optimisation, simulated quantum annealing) with their classical counterparts (genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimisation, simulated annealing), with general-purpose optimisers (differential evolution, L-SHADE, sep-CMA-ES, jSO, Gaussian QPSO, real-coded QEA, coordinate pattern search) and with mixed-integer linear programming (an exact MILP for the linear instances, a naive linearisation, a piecewise-linear MILP and its three-band and scenario-based forms). All optimisers receive the same number of objective-function evaluations and are tuned with one protocol.   Experiments - 21 synthetic day-ahead instances with 24 to 864 decision variables, 30 runs per algorithm and instance, evaluation budgets of 5,000, 20,000 and 100,000 - 1,311 data-driven day-ahead instances in three climates (typical-meteorological-year weather, measured electrical loads) - component ablations, budgets proportional to the number of variables, settings tuned at 864 variables - warm starts from the schedule of the piecewise-linear MILP - one year of rolling-horizon operation with 19 controllers, with and without a weekly demand charge, and three shorter variants (perfect forecasts, a second forecast-error model, random initialisation at every step)   Contents (143 files, 44 MB compressed) - qio_ies/: simulator of the energy system (numba), optimisers, MILP models, rolling-horizon operation - scripts/: one script per experiment, the statistical analysis, and the scripts that write the tables and figures - data/: processed measured load series - results/: output of every run (CSV, NPZ, JSON), reference costs and analysis tables - README.md: layout, commands and requirements   Reproduction The analysis tables and the tables and figures of the accompanying article can be regenerated from the stored run results with the analysis, table and figure scripts listed in README.md. The experiments themselves can be repeated with the run scripts. Metaheuristic runs are deterministic for a given seed. Extract the archive with the file times preserved.   Requirements Python 3.11 with numpy, scipy (HiGHS), numba, pandas, joblib, matplotlib and pvlib. The results were produced with Python 3.11.9, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, numba 0.66.0, pandas 3.0.3, matplotlib 3.11.0, joblib 1.5.3 and pvlib 0.15.2.   Data sources The weather records are the typical-meteorological-year files distributed with pvlib. The measured loads are derived from the UCI data set ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014 (https://doi.org/10.24432/C58C86).
title: Benchmark of quantum-inspired and classical metaheuristics and piecewise-linear MILP for PV–battery–heat-pump–thermal-storage scheduling: code, data and results

summary: Predictive world models learn to forecast observations, but accurate short-term predictions do not necessarily produce physically coherent behavior over longer horizons. We investigate how incorporating physical structure can strengthen world models while retaining their underlying predictive objectives. Across token-based models of planetary motion and JEPA-style visual models of mechanical systems, we study conserved-quantity supervision, symmetry-aware representations, temporal consistency, and learned structured dynamics. In planetary motion, angular-momentum supervision improves autonomous next-token forecasting, while the benefits of temporal regularization depend on the accompanying physical objective and representation. In visual models, generating rollouts through supervised energy-based dynamics heads produces more faithful trajectories and phase-space evolution. Together, these findings highlight the importance of how physical structure participates in prediction: improvements in an auxiliary physical readout or a local acceleration estimate do not automatically translate into more reliable long-horizon behavior. Evaluations across initial conditions and physical parameter shifts further reveal where these benefits persist and where generalization remains limited. Our study supports physical structure as a practical means of improving predictive world models and provides a unified framework for understanding its effects on representations, learned transitions, and autonomous rollouts. The central lesson is that effective physical inductive biases should help models both represent physical regularities and use them to generate future states.
title: Where Structure Enters a World Model: From Predictive Fit to Physical Rollout

direction_title: Memory Cortex: new source-grounded retrieval and continual-memory research [FORWARD]
summary: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at known tissue locations to reveal tissue organization and cellular function. Expression prediction requires modeling both local spatial relationships and associations among genes. Existing methods typically model expression using coordinate networks without explicit spatial parameterization. To address limited spatial sampling and sparse expression observations of ST, some methods firstly fit intermediate embeddings and then train expression predictors, but a latent representation suited to expression reconstruction may be difficult to predict from spatial coordinates. The two training stages can impose different demands on the latent representation. In this paper, we propose GaLF-ST, a Gaussian latent field method in which learnable Gaussian centers and anisotropic covariances determine the weights of latent vectors at each location. A shared nonlinear decoder maps their weighted average to multigene expression. In GaLF-ST, observed expression error jointly updates the Gaussian geometry, latent vectors, and decoder parameters. We further establish a unified benchmark across seven dataset groups and three held-out fractions, comparing GaLF-ST with four representative methods using the same locations, splits, gene panels, and scoring rules. Across tissues and observation densities, GaLF-ST achieves leading overall reconstruction performance, recovering spatial gene expression patterns and preserving tissue domains from limited observations while substantially reducing runtime and GPU memory usage.
title: GaLF-ST: Gaussian Latent Fields for Spatial Transcriptomics Reconstruction

direction_title: Memory Cortex: new source-grounded retrieval and continual-memory research [FORWARD]
summary: Long-tailed graph classification (LTGC) is common in real-world graph datasets, where a few large head graphs provide rich structural information while many smaller tail graphs offer fewer structural cues, making it harder to learn discriminative representations for tail graphs. To address this size-based imbalance, we propose Dynamic Memory-enhanced Pattern Relevance Prediction (DMPRP), which transfers structural patterns from head graphs to tail graphs. Given a graph representation as a query, a dynamic expert memory module inspired by Knowledge-diverse Experts (KDEX) generates a residual vector that augments the original representation. We train the module using co-occurrence triplets sampled from head graphs at the node, rooted subgraph, and random-walk neighborhood levels. Experiments on five graph classification benchmarks show that DMPRP improves tail performance, and ablation studies show that both the expert module and random-walk supervision contribute to these gains. A controlled experiment on PTC further examines pattern transfer when smaller graphs are denser than larger ones. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DMPRP-73A5.
title: Dynamic Memory-enhanced Pattern Relevance Prediction for Long-tailed Graph Classification

direction_title: Memory Cortex: new source-grounded retrieval and continual-memory research [FORWARD]
summary: Language models fuse reports in retrieval, multi-agent consensus and agent memory, where treating shared-source reports as independent can double count evidence. A common remedy is an instruction to count each source once. Its value depends on the receiver's raw baseline. Pricing it needs an exact reference. We build the graded-dependence exact reference: binary worlds with single-report reliability 0.65 and four dependence levels, whose disclosed parameters give every world an exact posterior and every rule a target risk. The paired gain protocol scores raw and instructed answers of four configurations on 2,976 worlds. Agreement and gain separate in both directions. At $δ$ = 0, claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6.1-sol agreed with the rule within 0.001 in 744 of 744, and the instruction raised their posterior mismatch by 0.044; gpt-6-luna agreed in 165 of 744 and gained 0.0140 (95% interval 0.0064 to 0.0219); claude-haiku-5-5's gain moved from -0.0295 ($δ$ = 0) to +0.0302 ($δ$ = 1) (descriptive). The prespecified first-child endpoint contrast, gain at $δ$ = 1 minus $δ$ = 0, was 0.0342 (0.0303 to 0.0382). In the preregistered tests, the raw source-weight contrast was positive (0.259, 95% interval 0.182 to 0.337; Holm rejected zero) and the grouping endpoint difference was not detected (0.0004, -0.0023 to 0.0031). This interval excludes differences larger than 0.0031 in magnitude and lies within the registered precision bound of $\pm$0.0046. The reference prices the rule before any model call. The paired gain, estimable as a Brier difference on labelled deployment items, decides adoption per receiver and prompt condition.
title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain
